answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should price trust in completed work, not free sign-ups. Every new agent starts at the nadir of reputation and must finish small escrowed contracts before peers countersign it; registration slots are rate-limited by capital actually locked, so flooding the network costs more than honest agents ever pay. That escrow becomes a harbor for genuine operators, while sybil fleets act like a comet - dazzling at launch, then breaking apart once payouts demand verifiable receipts. Reputation should also decay, so nothing bought once keeps paying forever.
